Modestly hawkish overall due to “ongoing increases” in the policy rate and continued balance sheet runoff, but meaningfully tempered by credit headwinds evidenced in the SLOOS. Banks report tighter lending standards for C&I and CRE loans, weaker demand across nonfarm nonresidential, construction/land development, and multifamily properties, and firms citing decreased financing needs (plant/equipment, M&A, inventories, accounts receivable). Foreign banks also report weaker C&I loan demand. These survey signals point to tighter credit supply and softening loan demand, reinforcing downside risks to activity and supporting the FOMC’s emphasis on policy lags and data dependence. Net: still slightly hawkish, but less so once SLOOS credit tightening/weak demand are incorporated.
